verbalization: Selegiline, a monoamine oxidase B (MAO-B) inhibitor, is implicated in the treatment of hemiparkinsonism-hemiatrophy syndrome, a condition associated with Juvenile Onset Parkinson Disease 19a. The evidence suggests that Selegiline may exert a therapeutic effect through a pathway involving the inhibition of MAO-B, which is linked to the pathophysiology of this disease. The observed relationships indicate that Selegiline could be repurposed for Juvenile Onset Parkinson Disease 19a, as it is associated with the same syndrome through different pathways—either via Droxidopa or Amantadine. These findings suggest that Selegiline may modulate the disease process by influencing neurotransmitter metabolism, potentially through MAO-B inhibition. The integrated evidence supports a mechanistic link between Selegiline and the disease, though further studies are needed to confirm the exact role of Selegiline in the pathogenesis of Juvenile Onset Parkinson Disease 19a.
